name: Release Management Conventions
description: This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on release management so output stays consistent and easy to review.
content:
This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on release management so output stays consistent and easy to review.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When release management decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
2. When release management guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
3. Measure before optimizing any release management bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
4. Document any non-obvious release management decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
5. Re-check edge cases relevant to release management (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
6. Keep release management outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
7. Prefer the simplest release management approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
8. Surface known limitations of a chosen release management approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
9. Check that release management terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting release management assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of release management correctness.
- Do not apply generic release management advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid mixing unrelated release management concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new release management abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these release management guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
